answer: Each identity must lock a slashable bond and complete a randomly timed interactive challenge in a tight window: the protocol issues a fresh nonce, and only a live signed response that cannot be precomputed counts. One operator cannot staff many windows at once, so a farm must keep a mesa of independent responders online. Trying to forge extra keys without extra labor misses the deadline and burns the bond. A public yarrow of missed-window slashes then bars cheap re-enrollment. Attacker cost scales with hired real-time attention and locked capital, not with the near-zero price of new keypairs.
